chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the weak ones (of understanding), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is the one who is not guided by a means to disbelief so that he would disbelieve, nor is he guided by a way to faith; he is not able to believe, nor is he able to disbelieve. So they are the children, and whoever of the men and women is upon the intellect of the children, the Pen (of recording deeds) is raised from them.'

key_terms.الْقَلَم: The Pen (symbolizing the recording of deeds)

ai.seo_question: Who are considered the 'weak ones' exempt from religious accountability in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) defines the 'weak ones' (al-mustad'af) not merely by age but by intellectual maturity, extending the exemption from religious accountability (taklif) to adults whose cognitive capacity resembles that of children. This definition aligns with the Shia juristic principle that the 'Pen' (qalam) is raised from those lacking the requisite 'ahl al-taklif' (capacity for obligation), emphasizing that accountability is contingent upon the maturity of the mind rather than biological age alone. The hadith thus provides a crucial criterion for determining the threshold of legal responsibility in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the weak ones (of understanding). So heasws said: ‘He is the one who is neither guided by a reason to the Kufr (disbelief) so he would disbelieve, nor is he guided by a way to the Emān. He neither has the capacity that he believes, nor does he have the capacity that he disbelieves. So they are children. And the ones from the men and the women who were upon a similar intellect of the children, the Pen (Recording of the deeds) would be Raised from them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from certain individuals of his people from Zurara who has said

the following: “Once I asked abu Ja’far (a.s.) about feeble-minded (weak) people. The Imam said, ‘They are those who have no means to become unbelievers and cannot find guidance to belief. They are not able to establish belief or to become unbelievers. Of such people are children and those of men and women who are of children’s mentality; the pen is held back from writing to hold them responsible.’”
